checks.name: article_type_gate_valid
details: classification evidence Abstract: 'We employed evolutionary and metabolic engineering in tandem to construct an Escherichia coli strain with improved GABA production' (a_b_s_t_r_a_c_t_p001) does not resolve
classification evidence Original Methods sections 4.1-4.12 describing strains, ALE, resequencing, mutant construction, assays, RNA-seq and qPCR performed by the authors does not resolve
classification evidence Original Results sections 2.2-2.7 with in-study measurements (Figs. 2-6, Tables 1-3) does not resolve

objective.value: Employ evolutionary engineering (adaptive laboratory evolution, ALE) and metabolic engineering in tandem to construct an Escherichia coli W-derived strain with improved gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) production using glycerol as the feedstock carbon, and to decipher the molecular basis of glycerol adaptation via mutation profiling, enzyme kinetics and transcriptome analysis.
objective.notes: Stated in Abstract; Discussion restates the primary focus as demonstrating applicability of evolutionary and metabolic engineering in tandem.

hypothesis.value: Adaptive evolution of E. coli W under glycerol limitation yields a strain with a metabolic system optimized for glycerol utilization, and leveraging this enhanced glycerol utilization (followed by rational inactivation of competing metabolic sinks ackA, mgsA and gabT) improves growth-coupled GABA production from glycerol compared with the wild-type.
hypothesis.notes: No explicit hypothesis statement exists in the available text; value is a bounded inference from the Abstract aim and the Results/Discussion logic (2.6-2.7, 3_discussion_p004).

inference.rationale: Abstract states the tandem engineering aim and the key drivers; 2_6/2_7 state the tests ('we examined whether such improvements translated into superior commodity metabolite production', 'we tested whether we could re-direct this metabolic flux to GABA production'); Discussion p004 states the primary focus. Combined, these delimit the implicit hypothesis without adding external content.

evolved_strain.role: single clone isolated from the fittest end-point lineage after 1300 generations of glycerol ALE

reverse_engineered_strains: reverse-engineered mglC mutant (Fig. S2, supplement unavailable)
gaba_production_strains: CY02 carrying the mtGAD GABA expression cassette
value.knockout_derivatives_in_wildtype: single and triple gene knockout derivatives of the wild-type lacZ:mtGAD strain (exact set per Fig. 6D/E and Fig. S8C/D; full list not enumerated in available text)

expression_host.role: protein overexpression host for GlpK purification only, not a target production strain

strain.notes: Complete strain/plasmid/primer list resides in Supplementary Table S3, which is not provided (dependency=requires_supplement). CY02 carrying mtGAD is inferred from GABA production measured in CY02 and the mention of the wild-type lacZ:mtGAD strain. ATCC 9637 appears only in a cited reference title and is not asserted here as the strain source.

value.CY02_new_mutations_count: 28 new mutations detected in CY02 after omitting parental background mutations (30 in the end-point population)

shared_notable_mutations.nucleotide_change: OCR-garbled in Table 1 ('8516 > A'); amino acid change reported

shared_notable_mutations.amino_acid_change: Gln 6* (table); text states 7th codon nonsense - see conflicts

value.gaba_cassette: mutant glutamate decarboxylase B (mtGAD) under inducible promoter PLtetQ-1, constitutively expressed due to absence of cognate repressor in E. coli W; cassette inserted into the chromosome (lacZ locus for the wild-type reference strain: 'lacZ:mtGAD')
value.knockouts: ΔackA, ΔmgsA, ΔgabT as single, double and triple combinations in CY02; single/triple knockouts also in wild-type background
value.expression_constructs: wild-type and mutant glpK cloned into pET28a(+) with N-terminal 6xHis tag for purification

genotype.notes: Only the 5 shared notable mutations are listed in available Table 1; the full set of 28 CY02 mutations and complete strain genotypes depend on unavailable Supplement (Fig. S1, Table S3). Table 1 is OCR-parsed; crp nucleotide change string is corrupted.

value: Adaptive laboratory evolution: serial batch transfer of E. coli W in M9 glycerol medium every 12 h for ~1300 generations with stepwise reduction of initial OD600 (0.0008 -> 0.0004 -> 0.00016); single-clone isolation on M9 glycerol agar
Whole-genome resequencing (Illumina MiSeq, 50-cycle single-end) for mutation profiling
lambda-Red recombinase-mediated reverse engineering of point mutations (Datsenko and Wanner 2000)

lambda-Red gene knockout: target replacement by KanR cassette amplified from pKD13, electroporation (1.8 kV, 0.1 cm cuvette) into pKD46-containing cells, selection on 50 ug/mL kanamycin, marker excision via pCP20, curing at 42 degC
Chromosomal insertion of the mtGAD GABA expression cassette (PLtetQ-1 promoter, constitutive in E. coli W)
Medium/feedstock optimization: switch from M9 minimal (0.2% v/v glycerol + 50 mg/L yeast extract) to LB + 2% (v/v) glycerol, glycerol concentration selected by growth-rate proxy
engineering_method.notes: Section 4.4 explicitly describes the knockout procedure; point-mutation reverse engineering is stated in 2_3_p001 to use the lambda-Red method but its detailed protocol is not separately described in the available text (likely Supplementary Table S3 dependency).

knockout_screen_WT_background: wild-type lacZ:mtGAD and its single/triple knockout derivatives

experimental_groups.notes: Groups are bound per experiment instance in experimental_design_object; this projection enumerates distinct group sets without merging conditions across experiments.

value.fitness_uptake_cAMP_acetate_GABA: parental E. coli W wild-type as comparator in each corresponding experiment
value.enzyme_kinetics: wild-type GlpK (GlpK^w) purified from the parental strain as control for GlpK T235M
value.knockout_specificity: wild-type lacZ:mtGAD knockout derivatives used to test whether knockout effects are intrinsic to E. coli W or specific to the evolved CY02 background
value.rna_seq: wild-type E. coli W as reference for differential expression

controls.notes: No exogenous negative/blank controls (e.g., empty-vector or no-template controls) are explicitly reported in the available text.

value.flask_culture: 50 mL culture in 250 mL Erlenmeyer flasks at 37 degC, 200 rpm; growth profile sampled every 2 h (Figs. 1 and 5)
value.ale: 50 mL M9 glycerol medium in 250 mL Erlenmeyer flat-bottom flask, 37 degC with agitation; batch cultures transferred to fresh medium every 12 h
value.plate_reader_growth: EPOCH2 plate reader, 37 degC, 807 rpm double orbital shaking, 24 h, 96-well default configuration, 110 uL working volume, OD600 every 10 min (Fig. S7)
value.glycerol_acetate_sampling: 50 mL M9 glycerol in 250 mL flasks; after 1.5 h incubation, 1.5 mL collected at 1 h intervals during exponential phase
value.rna_seq_culture: M9 minimal medium + 2 g/L glycerol; harvest at OD600 0.4-0.5
value.protein_expression: 200 mL LB + 50 ug/mL kanamycin at 37 degC; induction with 1 mM IPTG

culture_conditions.notes: Temperature values are bound to their process steps (cultivation 37 degC vs enzyme assay 25 degC vs HPLC oven 37/49/30 degC); they are not interchangeable.

value.default: M9 minimal medium (BD) supplemented with 0.2% (v/v) glycerol, or Luria Bertani (LB) medium unless stated otherwise
value.gaba_minimal: M9 glycerol (0.2% v/v) minimal medium supplemented with 50 mg/L yeast extract
value.ale: M9 glycerol medium (0.2% v/v glycerol); M9 glycerol agar for clone isolation
value.rna_seq: M9 minimal medium supplemented with 2 g/L pure glycerol

medium.notes: Exact M9 salts composition is not itemized in the available text.

value.yeast_extract: 50 mg/L in minimal medium used for GABA production
value.enzyme_assay: 0.5 ug/mL of each GlpK enzyme per 200 uL reaction; FBP titrated 0-10 mM for allosteric assays

dosage.notes: Dosages are bound to distinct subsystems (culture carbon source, selection, induction, in vitro assay); no induction dose applies to the mtGAD cassette because expression is constitutive in E. coli W.

value.ale_duration: ~1300 generations under glycerol limitation; transfers every 12 h
value.growth_profiling: every 2 h intervals (flask); every 10 min for 24 h (plate reader, Fig. S7)
value.glycerol_acetate_sampling: 1 h intervals during exponential growth after 1.5 h incubation
value.gaba_time_course: over 24 h; stationary-phase endpoint measurements also reported

time.notes: Absolute calendar duration of the ALE campaign is not stated; only generations and transfer interval are reported.

value.glpK_specific_activity_fig2D: six replicates for wild-type enzyme, five replicates for mutant enzyme (replicate type not further specified in caption)
value.cAMP_fig3B: biological triplicates measured in technical duplicates
value.rt_qpcr: two biological replicates, each with three technical replicates

replicates.notes: Replicate counts derive from figure captions and Methods; figure images were not visually inspectable. Enzyme-assay replicate type (biological vs technical) is not specified in the caption. Fig. 1 caption is missing, so ALE replicate/lineage count (single lineage vs parallel lines) is unknown.

value: Specific growth rate from OD600 time series
Glycerol consumption and acetate secretion quantification (Cedex Bio Analyzer with Glycerol Bio Test and Acetate V2 Bio Test kits; rates per Eq. 2-3)
GlpK catalytic and allosteric (FBP inhibition) kinetic assays (coupled pyruvate kinase/lactate dehydrogenase, A340 decrease, Eq. 4 fit)
Intracellular cAMP enzyme-linked immunoassay (Invitrogen kit)
RT-qPCR of glpK transcript (normalized to rrsA or ihfB)
RNA-seq differential expression (DESeq2)
GABA quantification: HPLC-UV (Primesep 100, 215 nm) for M9 supernatants; dansyl chloride derivatization HPLC-UV (Zorbax Eclipse C18, 286 nm) for LB supernatants
Time-course glycerol by HPLC-RID (MetaCarb 87H)
Whole-genome resequencing for mutation identification
Sanger sequencing validation of cloned glpK; SDS-PAGE monitoring of purified protein
EPOCH2 microplate reader/spectrophotometer (BioTek) - growth curves and GlpK kinetics
Cedex Bio Analyzer (Roche) - glycerol/acetate quantification
MiSeq (Illumina) with MiSeq Reagent Kit v2 - genome resequencing
HiSeq (Illumina) - RNA-seq
Nexera LC-40 HPLC system with RID-20A RI detector and UV detector (Shimadzu); columns: MetaCarb 87H (Agilent), Primesep 100 (Sielc), Zorbax Eclipse C18 (Agilent)
StepOnePlus Real-Time PCR System (Applied Biosystems)
MicroPulser electroporator (Bio-Rad)
Qubit 2.0 fluorometer (ThermoFisher); TapeStation 2200 (Agilent)
Econo-Pac chromatography column with Ni-NTA agarose; float-A-Lyzer G2 dialysis device (Repligen)
Independent t-test (growth rate and GUR comparisons, Fig. 2A/B)
One-way ANOVA with Tukey's post hoc test (cAMP, Fig. 3B; acetate secretion, Fig. 4B)
DESeq2: DEG thresholds fold change > 2 and adjusted P-value < 0.01
CLC Genomics Workbench read trimming (quality limit 0.05, discard >2 ambiguous nt) and mapping to NC_017635.1 (mismatch cost 2, indel cost 3, length/similarity 0.9)
Curve fitting with SigmaPlot 12; allosteric inhibition fit per Eq. (4) (K0.5, Hill coefficient)
Generation number from initial/final cell densities per Eq. (1)
Glycerol consumption and acetate secretion rates per Eq. (2)-(3) (Heyland et al., 2009)
qPCR analysis with StepOne Software v2.3; primer efficiency from 10^1-10^4-fold gDNA standard curve; normalization to rrsA or ihfB
Gen 5 software for plate-reader output
CRP regulon enrichment analysis against RegulonDB annotation

value.ale: CY02 specific growth rate in minimal glycerol improved ~40% (0.67 +/- 0.03 to 0.94 +/- 0.01 /hr), comparable to wild-type on glucose (0.87 +/- 0.04 /hr); glycerol consumption rate significantly increased; fitness gain on glucose negligible (glycerol-specific adaptation)
value.mutation_profiling: 93 mutations in end-point population, 89 in CY02; 30 and 28 new mutations after background subtraction; shared notable mutations in glpK (T235M), crp (R209H), ptsP, rsfS, mglC
value.reverse_engineering_fitness: significant growth-rate increases for glpK^m (1.45-fold), glpK^m crp^m (1.56-fold), CY02 (1.63-fold); crp^m not significant; GUR increased in glpK^m-harboring strains (1.78/1.70/1.60-fold), not in crp^m; mglC mutant growth unchanged (hitchhiker, Fig. S2 unavailable)
value.enzyme_kinetics: GlpK T235M catalytic activity unchanged vs WT but insensitive to FBP inhibition (FBP K0.5: WT 0.386 mM per text; mutant >10,000 uM per Table 2); Table 2 OCR partially garbled - see conflicts
value.cAMP: glpK^m-harboring strains ~2% of wild-type cAMP (~98% decrease); CY02 ~20% of WT; crp^m 36% of WT; all significant (P<0.001)
value.glpK_expression: glpK mRNA 3-6% of WT in glpK^m-harboring strains incl. CY02; ~22% in crp^m; double mutant less than half of glpK^m (Fig. S4 unavailable)
value.transcriptome: 640 DEGs (149 up, 491 down) in CY02 vs WT; 181 CRP-regulated DEGs; 148/157 positively regulated CRP genes downregulated; lower glycolysis up, TCA/respiration/ATP synthase down, pta/ackA up, acs down
value.acetate: acetate secretion far above detection limit in CY02 and glpK^m-harboring mutants; not determinable for WT and crp^m
value.gaba_minimal: no meaningful difference in M9 glycerol: 0.06 +/- 0.01 g/L for both WT and CY02
value.gaba_timecourse: max titer WT 0.15 +/- 0.01 g/L and productivity 0.03 +/- 0.01 g/L/hr; CY02 0.39 +/- 0.03 g/L and 0.08 +/- 0.01 g/L/hr (~2.6-fold increase); glycerol consumption similar
value.knockouts: single KOs lower than comparator; double KOs 0.46 +/- 0.02 (ΔgabTΔackA), 0.45 +/- 0.01 (ΔgabTΔmgsA), 0.37 +/- 0.04 g/L (ΔmgsAΔackA); CY02_TKO 0.59 +/- 0.04 g/L and 0.13 +/- 0.02 g/L/hr (1.5-/1.6-fold over CY02; 3.9-/4.3-fold over WT); WT-background deletions generally lowered GABA and the double/triple KO benefit was not observed in WT background
value.growth_effect_of_knockouts: knockouts did not affect growth rate; ΔackA-containing strains showed prolonged lag phase

outcomes.notes: Values compiled from Results text, embedded tables and figure captions without merging across conditions. Fig. 1 caption missing; Fig. S1-S8 and Supplementary Tables unavailable, so several referenced quantitative details (e.g., Fig. S2 mglC data, Fig. S7 growth screen, Fig. S8 KO profiles) cannot be verified from the provided content.

experiments.title: Adaptive laboratory evolution of E. coli W under glycerol limitation
experiments.intervention: serial batch cultivation in 50 mL M9 glycerol (0.2% v/v) medium, 250 mL flask, 37 degC with agitation, transfer every 12 h, initial OD600 stepwise 0.0008 -> 0.0004 -> 0.00016, ~1300 generations (Eq. 1)
experiments.replicates: unknown (Fig. 1 caption missing; number of parallel lineages not stated in available text)
experiments.readouts: estimated doubling time over generations (Fig. 1B), specific growth rate (Fig. 1C), glycerol consumption rate (Fig. 1D)
experiments.outcomes: single clone CY02 isolated; growth rate 0.67 +/- 0.03 -> 0.94 +/- 0.01 /hr (~40% increase); increased glycerol consumption rate; negligible fitness change on glucose
experiments.notes: Results text for this experiment is embedded in paragraph 1_introduction_p003 due to a parser section-misattribution; Fig. 1 caption absent.

experiments.title: Whole-genome resequencing and causal-mutation nomination
experiments.readouts: mutation calls vs NC_017635.1 after parental background subtraction
experiments.analysis: shared-mutation focus between population and CY02 (Table 1, Fig. S1)
experiments.outcomes: 93 (population) / 89 (CY02) total mutations; 30 / 28 new; shared notable: glpK T235M, crp R209H, ptsP Pro174fs, rsfS Gln6*, mglC Asn4fs

experiments.title: Reverse engineering of glpK^m/crp^m and fitness/GUR characterization
experiments.intervention: lambda-Red recombinase-mediated introduction of glpK T235M and crp R209H singly and in combination into parental W
experiments.conditions: M9 minimal glycerol medium; exponential growth
experiments.readouts: specific growth rate (Fig. 2A), specific glycerol uptake rate (Fig. 2B, Cedex)
experiments.outcomes: growth: glpK^m 1.45-fold (p<0.022), double 1.56-fold (p=0.037), CY02 1.63-fold (p=0.009), crp^m n.s.; GUR: 1.78/1.70/1.60-fold for glpK^m strains, crp^m n.s.

experiments.title: GlpK^w vs GlpK T235M expression, purification and enzyme kinetics
experiments.intervention: cloning of WT/mutant glpK into pET28a(+) (N-terminal 6xHis), overexpression in BL21(DE3), Ni-NTA purification
experiments.conditions: assay at 25 degC, pH 7.0, 200 uL reaction, 0.5 ug/mL enzyme; FBP 0-10 mM for allostery
experiments.replicates: six replicates (WT enzyme), five replicates (mutant enzyme) per Fig. 2D caption; replicate type unspecified
experiments.readouts: V0/Vmax, specific activity vs FBP; Vmax, Km_gly, kcat, kcat/Km, FBP K0.5 (Table 2)
experiments.analysis: SigmaPlot 12 curve fitting; Eq. (4) allosteric fit
experiments.outcomes: catalytic activity unchanged; mutant insensitive to FBP (K0.5 >10,000 uM vs 0.386 mM WT per text)

experiments.title: Intracellular cAMP measurement
experiments.conditions: exponential phase harvest; ice-cold 65% ethanol extraction
experiments.analysis: one-way ANOVA with Tukey's post hoc
experiments.outcomes: glpK^m-harboring strains ~2% of WT; CY02 ~20% of WT; crp^m 36% of WT; all P<0.001

experiments.title: RT-qPCR of glpK expression
experiments.controls: wild-type; normalization to rrsA or ihfB
experiments.readouts: relative glpK mRNA abundance (Fig. S4, unavailable)
experiments.analysis: StepOne Software v2.3; standard-curve primer efficiency
experiments.outcomes: glpK^m-harboring strains 3-6% of WT; crp^m ~22%; double mutant < half of glpK^m

experiments.title: RNA-seq transcriptome comparison WT vs CY02
experiments.conditions: M9 minimal + 2 g/L glycerol; harvest OD600 0.4-0.5
experiments.readouts: gene expression; DEGs; CRP regulon enrichment
experiments.analysis: CLC Genomics Workbench trimming/mapping; DESeq2 (FC>2, adj P<0.01)
experiments.outcomes: 640 DEGs (149 up / 491 down); 181 CRP-regulated DEGs; 148/157 positively regulated CRP genes downregulated; lower glycolysis up, TCA/respiration down, pta/ackA up, acs down

experiments.title: Acetate secretion rate measurement
experiments.analysis: one-way ANOVA with Tukey's post hoc
experiments.outcomes: WT below accurate determination; CY02 and glpK^m-harboring mutants elevated; crp^m not determinable

experiments.title: GABA production in M9 glycerol minimal medium
experiments.conditions: 50 mL M9 glycerol (0.2% v/v) + 50 mg/L yeast extract, 250 mL flasks, biological triplicates
experiments.outcomes: 0.06 +/- 0.01 g/L for both WT and CY02 (negligible difference)

experiments.title: Medium and glycerol-concentration optimization for GABA production
experiments.intervention: switch to amino acid-rich LB + glycerol; glycerol concentration screen using growth rate as proxy (Fig. S7, plate reader)

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Current authors designed and executed an ALE campaign (serial batch transfer under glycerol limitation with stepwise OD600 reduction) as an active strain-engineering intervention; passes Q1 (evolution/selection campaign), Q2 (this study), Q3 (deliberate design choice of selection regime).
ddr_annotations.design_action: Adaptive laboratory evolution of E. coli W in M9 glycerol (0.2% v/v) with 12 h serial transfers and stepwise lowering of initial OD600 (0.0008 -> 0.0004 -> 0.00016) for ~1300 generations, followed by single-clone isolation (CY02)
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Selection for fastest-growing progeny under glycerol limitation to optimize the metabolic system for glycerol utilization
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Glycerol is a non-preferential, low-energy-density carbon source and wild-type E. coli metabolic networks are not optimized for glycerol utilization; E. coli W is a fast-growing, stress-tolerant industrial platform with high GABA production on glycerol reported previously (Hou and Kang, 2018)
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=literature_precedent: the decision rests on prior ALE demonstrations and prior strain characterization rather than on new measurements made before the action in this study
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: ALE under glycerol limitation repeatedly improved glycerol growth in prior E. coli studies (cited: Ibarra 2002, Fong 2005, Herring 2006, Cheng 2014, Kang 2019); authors apply the established approach to E. coli W

generalizable_rule.rule: Serial-batch ALE under glycerol limitation (~1300 generations, 12 h transfers, decreasing inoculum OD) can improve glycerol-utilization fitness of E. coli W, yielding clones with ~40% higher specific growth rate on minimal glycerol
generalizable_rule.scope: strain improvement of E. coli W for glycerol utilization by batch ALE
excluded_scope: other E. coli strains or species
direct improvement of any specific product titer (GABA improvement required additional steps)

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Authors actively chose which ALE-derived mutations to reconstruct (glpK^m, crp^m, and the double; mglC also reconstructed) in the parental background via lambda-Red recombineering to test causality; passes Q1-Q3.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Reverse engineering of glpK Thr235Met and crp Arg209His, singly and combined, into parental E. coli W using the lambda-Red recombinase-mediated method
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: glpK and crp mutations are recurrent under glycerol/nutrient limitation in prior ALEs and were shared between the end-point population and CY02; mglC was tested and showed no fitness effect (hitchhiker); rsfS and ptsP were deprioritized based on low recurrence and conflicting literature
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: WGS of parental strain, end-point population and CY02 identified 30/28 new mutations with a shared set including glpK, crp, ptsP, rsfS, mglC (Table 1)
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=experimental_measurement (WGS of this study) combined with literature_precedent on mutation recurrence
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Selection of glpK/crp as candidate causal mutations explicitly rests on their recurrence across prior glycerol/nutrient-limitation ALE studies; mglC exclusion rests on this study's reverse-engineering result

generalizable_rule.rule: Introducing the ALE-derived glpK T235M mutation into parental E. coli W increases specific growth rate (~1.45-fold) and glycerol uptake rate (~1.78-fold) in minimal glycerol medium, consistent with loss of FBP-mediated allosteric inhibition of glycerol kinase
generalizable_rule.scope: causal contribution of the specific glpK T235M allele in the E. coli W background under glycerol limitation
tested_scope: glpK T235M alone or with crp R209H
excluded_scope: other carbon sources or cultivation modes
generalizable_rule.evidence_basis: EXP03 and EXP04 outcomes; reason nature literature_analogy with in-study experimental measurement

alternatives_considered: mglC mutation: reverse-engineered but specific growth rate unchanged vs wild-type (Fig. S2), treated as hitchhiker
rsfS nonsense mutation: low recurrence in ALE databases, not pursued
ptsP frame-shift: conflicting literature on fitness role, not pursued

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Use of a chromosomally inserted mtGAD cassette (PLtetQ-1, constitutive in E. coli W) as the GABA-producing module; Q1 and Q3 pass. Q2 is partially uncertain: the Abstract states 'we constructed a GABA-producing E. coli W-derivative', but the mtGAD strain may derive from the group's earlier work (Hou and Kang, 2018); construction details are in unavailable Supplementary Table S3.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Chromosomal insertion of the mutant glutamate decarboxylase B (mtGAD) expression cassette under PLtetQ-1 (lacZ:mtGAD in the wild-type reference), enabling constitutive expression without antibiotic markers
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: mtGAD is catalytically active at physiological pH, unlike wild-type GAD, making it the enzyme of choice for fermentative GABA production (cited: Choi 2015, Thu Ho 2013, Hou and Kang 2018); chromosomal insertion precludes antibiotic use during culture
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Prior demonstration that E. coli W achieved among the highest GABA production on glycerol feedstock (Hou and Kang, 2018); need for a GABA-producing module to test whether ALE improvements translate into production
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=literature_precedent for enzyme choice; attribution of the construction step to this study vs the prior Hou and Kang 2018 study is uncertain (requires Supplementary Table S3)
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Enzyme and expression-mode choices are justified by cited prior studies rather than new mechanistic evidence generated before the decision in this paper
alternatives_considered: plasmid-based expression with strong promoters (noted as common practice; chromosomal expression chosen, precluding antibiotic markers - stated as design rationale, comparison with plasmid systems appears only post hoc in Discussion)

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Authors changed the production medium from M9 minimal (0.2% glycerol + 50 mg/L yeast extract) to LB + 2% (v/v) glycerol and selected the glycerol concentration via a growth-rate proxy screen; an active, implemented process-design choice (Q1-Q3 pass).
ddr_annotations.design_action: Replacement of minimal medium with amino acid-rich LB supplemented with 2% (v/v) glycerol as sole carbon source for GABA production; glycerol concentration optimized using specific growth rate as proxy under the assumption of growth-coupled production
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Prior reports that amino acid supplementation restores growth efficiency and substrate-to-biomass conversion (cited: Prensky 2021, Russell and Cook 1995, Waschina 2016); several prior GABA studies used >=10 g/L carbon feedstock
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Measured final GABA concentrations in M9 glycerol minimal medium were negligible and identical between wild-type and CY02 (0.06 +/- 0.01 g/L each), despite CY02's enhanced glycerol utilization
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=experimental_measurement (EXP09 null result in minimal medium, preceding the change) plus literature_precedent for amino acid supplementation; the growth-coupled proxy assumption is an author assumption requiring caution
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: The medium-switch rationale is grounded in cited literature on growth inefficiency and amino acid supplementation, applied to this system after the in-study null result

generalizable_rule.rule: For growth-coupled GABA production from glycerol in E. coli W (WT and glycerol-adapted derivatives), amino acid-rich LB medium with 2% (v/v) glycerol yields substantially higher GABA titers than M9 minimal medium with 0.2% glycerol and 50 mg/L yeast extract
generalizable_rule.scope: medium choice for growth-coupled GABA fermentation from glycerol in E. coli W backgrounds
tested_scope: E. coli W WT, glpK^m, crp^m, glpK^m crp^m, CY02
LB + 2% (v/v) glycerol vs M9 + 0.2% glycerol + 50 mg/L yeast extract
excluded_scope: other hosts, products or carbon sources
glycerol concentrations outside the tested screen (Fig. S7 unavailable)

alternatives_considered: continued use of M9 minimal + 0.2% glycerol + 50 mg/L yeast extract (tested; negligible GABA, abandoned)
other glycerol concentrations screened by growth-rate proxy (Fig. S7); 2% (v/v) selected as giving highest specific growth rate

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Rational, targeted inactivation of ackA, mgsA and gabT (singles, doubles, triple) in CY02 to redirect flux from acetate overflow and competing sinks toward GABA; active design choice implemented in this study (Q1-Q3 pass).
ddr_annotations.design_action: lambda-Red-mediated deletion of ackA (acetate kinase), mgsA (methylglyoxal synthase) and gabT (GABA transaminase) individually and in combination in CY02, yielding CY02_ΔackA, CY02_ΔgabT, CY02_ΔmgsA, double knockouts and CY02_TKO; parallel deletions in the wild-type lacZ:mtGAD background as specificity control
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: ackA: re-route carbon lost as acetate overflow; mgsA: curb cytotoxic methylglyoxal accumulation expected from FBP-insensitive glpK mutants and remove a lactate-yielding auxiliary pathway; gabT: block GABA shunt re-entry into TCA, a common GABA-production practice (cited: Pham 2015/2016, Mazumdar 2013, Freedberg 1971, Im 2020, Le Vo 2012/2013, Luo 2021, Zhao 2017)
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Prior in-study observation of pronounced aerobic acetate overflow in CY02 and glpK^m-harboring mutants (EXP08, Fig. 4B) and upregulated pta/ackA with downregulated acs in CY02 transcriptome (EXP07), together with literature on methylglyoxal toxicity of glpK mutants
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=experimental_measurement (acetate overflow and transcriptome measured in this study before the knockouts) combined with literature_precedent for target selection
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Target selection is justified by a pathway-level mechanistic model (overflow flux redirection, methylglyoxal detoxification, GABA shunt blockage) anchored in this study's measurements; however, the beneficial triple-knockout outcome is attributed by the authors to unknown epistatic interactions in the CY02 background, so the mechanistic basis of the final improvement is only partially explained

generalizable_rule.rule: In the glycerol-adapted E. coli W CY02 background, combined deletion of ackA, mgsA and gabT increases GABA titer and specific productivity (~1.5- and ~1.6-fold over CY02; 0.59 +/- 0.04 g/L and 0.13 +/- 0.02 g/L/hr), whereas the same deletions do not improve production in the wild-type background, indicating genetic-background dependence (epistasis)
generalizable_rule.scope: flux-redirection knockout design for GABA production in glycerol-adapted E. coli W
tested_scope: ackA/mgsA/gabT single, double and triple deletions
wild-type lacZ:mtGAD background as comparator (no benefit)
excluded_scope: wild-type or non-evolved E. coli backgrounds (tested, benefit not observed)
other hosts, products, carbon sources or scales
mechanistic attribution of the epistatic effect (unknown per authors)
generalizable_rule.evidence_basis: EXP08/EXP07 trigger measurements and EXP12 outcomes; reason nature mechanistic_inference

alternatives_considered: single and double knockout combinations (constructed and tested; single KOs lowered GABA, doubles intermediate, triple highest)
other unnamed knockout targets considered among 'many knockout targets'; the three chosen per stated rationale

design_logic.summary: Top-down ALE for glycerol adaptation (DDR01) -> mutation identification and causal validation by reverse engineering (DDR02) -> chromosomal mtGAD production module (DDR03, attribution to this study partially uncertain) -> medium/feedstock optimization after null result in minimal medium (DDR04) -> rational metabolic-sink knockouts triggered by observed acetate overflow (DDR05).
